newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close higher, snap losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close higher, snap losing streak.

text.p: Mexican stocks broke a run of four consecutive falls to close higher Wednesday after foreign buyers stepped in to pick up shares made very cheap in the wake of a recent slide by the peso, traders said.
"I liked the fact that volume picked up today. Although gains weren't very juicy, many shares were attractively priced," said Gerardo Copca, deputy research director at the Arka brokerage.
The blue-chip IPC index closed up 11.48 points, or 0.36 percent, at 3,263.01.
Technical analysts said the IPC gained after bottoming out at 3,212.14 points and thereby respecting a support they located at 3,200 points.
"The market rebounded well at 3,200 points, and tomorrow may see us at 3,300," an analyst said.
Traders pointed out, however, that the market was still very cautious over very volatile exchange and interest rates.

"You can't avoid jitters with such a weak peso. People are postponing (third-quarter earnings) reports and macro data until after it is clear where the peso and Cetes (bond) will end up," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso earlier staggered to 11.6 centavos weaker at 7.8250/7.8450 per dollar, before clawing back some lost ground to close at 7.7800/7.7850.

The peso weakened despite hefty primary rate hikes at Tuesday night's primary auction, where Banco de Mexico had assigned the bellwether 28-day Cetes rate at 25.90 percent, or 3.16 percentage points above last week's rate.
Official preliminary figures showing that August's industrial output was up 12.7 percent from year-ago figures failed to move the cautious market.
Volume did improve over many recent sessions, however, to 99.3 million shares traded.

Traders pointed out that the weakening peso favoured exporting companies, such as industrial combine Alfa, whose A series shares gained 75 centavos (10 cents) to 33.05 pesos ($4.24), and steelmakers Hylsamex BCP series, up 50 centavos (6 cents) to 29.00 pesos ($3.72), and Ahmsa, whose nominal shares closed up 24 centavos (3 cents) to 19.90 pesos ($2.56).
Of 102 stocks that changed hands, gainers outnumbered losers by 41 to 38, with the remaining 23 unchanged.
